catalogue.blocks.lm7805_5v_supply.descri: An LM7805 from 12 V with 330 nF input and 100 nF output capacitors, loaded with 100 mA.
catalogue.blocks.lm7805_5v_supply.notes: A linear regulator burns (12 − 5) V × current as heat: 0.7 W here, but 0.5 A would exceed its free-air limit. RL stands in for the circuit being powered; on a real board it needs 1 W.
catalogue.blocks.lm7805_5v_supply.name: 12 V to 5 V supply (7805)
catalogue.blocks.lm1117_3v3_supply.descr: An LM1117-3.3 low-dropout regulator with 10 µF input and output capacitors, loaded with 100 mA.
catalogue.blocks.lm1117_3v3_supply.notes: Dissipation is (5 − 3.3) V × load current: 0.17 W at 100 mA. C2 must be electrolytic or tantalum: the LM1117 needs 0.3–22 Ω output ESR to stay stable, too high for a ceramic (datasheet p.15). RL stands in for the circuit being powered.
catalogue.blocks.lm1117_3v3_supply.name: 5 V to 3.3 V supply (LM1117)
catalogue.blocks.opamp_noninverting_gain: A non-inverting MCP6002 stage on 3.3 V: gain = 1 + RF/RG = 2, so 0.8 V in gives 1.6 V out.
Keep the output below the supply: input × gain must stay under about 3.25 V here. CB is the supply bypass the datasheet asks for: place it within 2 mm of pin 8 (datasheet p.14).
catalogue.blocks.opamp_buffer_3v3.descri: An MCP6002 rail-to-rail op-amp on 3.3 V buffers a 1.65 V divider so a load can't pull it down.
catalogue.blocks.opamp_buffer_3v3.notes: Swap the divider for your sensor; the follower's output tracks its input with almost no load on it. CB is the supply bypass the datasheet asks for: place it within 2 mm of pin 8 (datasheet p.14).
catalogue.blocks.opamp_buffer_3v3.name: Op-amp voltage follower (3.3 V)
catalogue.blocks.opamp_buffer_3v3.expect: the output follows the 1.65 V divider
catalogue.blocks.pwm_rc_filter.descripti: Pi GPIO18 PWM at 1 kHz, 50 % through a 10 kΩ / 1 µF low-pass filter (τ = 10 ms) gives about 1.65 V.
catalogue.blocks.pwm_rc_filter.notes: Larger RC means less ripple but slower response; buffer the output with an op-amp for loads.
catalogue.blocks.pwm_rc_filter.name: PWM to analog voltage
catalogue.blocks.pi_npn_led_switch.descr: Pi GPIO17 switches a 5 V, 15 mA LED through a 2N3904, so the pin only supplies ~0.3 mA.
catalogue.blocks.pi_npn_led_switch.notes: Base resistor 10 kΩ keeps pin current tiny; the 200 Ω collector resistor sets LED current.
catalogue.blocks.pi_npn_led_switch.name: NPN switch for a brighter LED
catalogue.blocks.pi_npn_led_switch.expec: the Pi pin sources only about 0.25 mA
catalogue.blocks.pi_relay_driver.descrip: Pi GPIO17 switches a 12 V coil (400 Ω, 100 mH) through a logic-level IRLZ44N, with a 1N5819 flyback diode, 100 Ω gate resistor and 100 kΩ pull-down.
catalogue.blocks.pi_relay_driver.notes: Delete the flyback diode and simulate to see the drain spike fail the MOSFET's rating.
catalogue.blocks.pi_relay_driver.name: Relay or solenoid driver
catalogue.blocks.pi_relay_driver.expecta: coil current reaches 12 V / 400 Ω = 30 mA
the flyback diode clamps the drain near 12 V
catalogue.footprints.L.axial.note: Small signal inductor; a relay or solenoid coil is off-board

part_ratings.rating_warnings.parts_are_c: Parts are checked against their absolute maximums: peak voltage and current on the solver's own timepoints, and time-averaged power over this run. Resistors use their package's typical power and working voltage; capacitors their chosen voltage rating, and electrolytics must never see reverse voltage. Inductor current and saturation, and sources, are not checked.
part_ratings.rating_warnings.device_curr: Device current is measured into terminal 0 (drain, collector or output); BJT power omits the small base term. Op-amps and regulators are behavioral models and do not current-limit: an iout_max failure means the real part would limit or fail.
part_ratings.rating_warnings.board_pins_: Board pins are modelled at their default drive with ESD clamp diodes to the logic rail and ground; firmware behaviour is not simulated. The board's GND is the circuit ground.
part_ratings.rating_warnings.draft_parts: Draft parts ({{parts}}): models and ratings are unconfirmed against datasheets, so a pass is not hardware approval.
passive_ratings.capacitor_advice.has_no_: {{part}} has no voltage rating, so it is not checked. It sees up to {{peak}} V in this run: choose at least {{rating}} V (1.5x the peak; ceramics lose capacitance near their rating, so 2x is safer for them).
support_checks.rule_finding.is_ceramic_w: {{capacitors}} is ceramic, which this part cannot use here; choose an electrolytic (radial) or tantalum.

catalogue.support.lm324.1.purpose: the datasheet asks for a low-ESR bypass without a value; 0.1 µF is the usual choice (dual supply: each rail)
catalogue.support.lm358.0.purpose: a low-ESR ceramic bypass right at the supply pin keeps supply noise out
catalogue.support.lm358.1.purpose: a low-ESR ceramic bypass right at the supply pin keeps supply noise out (dual supply: each rail)
catalogue.support.mcp6002.0.purpose: a 0.01–0.1 µF bypass within 2 mm, plus a shared ≥ 1 µF bulk capacitor within 100 mm
catalogue.support.mcp6002.1.purpose: a 0.01–0.1 µF bypass within 2 mm, plus a shared ≥ 1 µF bulk capacitor within 100 mm (dual supply: each rail)
catalogue.support.tl072.0.purpose: a low-ESR ceramic bypass right at the supply pin keeps supply noise out
catalogue.support.tl072.1.purpose: a low-ESR ceramic bypass right at the supply pin keeps supply noise out (dual supply: each rail)
catalogue.support.lm1117_3v3.0.purpose: for stability; its ESR must be 0.3–22 Ω (TI specifies tantalum), so a ceramic is too low
catalogue.support.lm1117_3v3.1.purpose: an input capacitor; TI suggests 10 µF tantalum
catalogue.support.lm317.0.purpose: an input bypass for stability when the regulator is more than about 15 cm from the supply's filter capacitors, which is always true when the supply arrives through a connector
catalogue.support.lm317.1.purpose: improves transient response; not needed for stability
catalogue.support.lm7805.0.purpose: an input bypass for stability when the regulator is more than about 15 cm from the supply's filter capacitors, which is always true when the supply arrives through a connector
catalogue.support.lm7805.1.purpose: improves transient response; place it close to the pins
catalogue.support.lm7812.0.purpose: an input bypass for stability when the regulator is more than about 15 cm from the supply's filter capacitors, which is always true when the supply arrives through a connector
catalogue.support.lm7812.1.purpose: improves transient response; place it close to the pins
catalogue.support.mcp1700_3v3.0.purpose: for small-signal stability; ESR 0–2 Ω, so ceramic is fine
catalogue.support.mcp1700_3v3.1.purpose: a low source impedance at the input keeps the LDO stable
